video_title: Why HTTP Wins at the Edge Even Though It's Inefficient
core_insight: HTTP is a stateless, uniform resource contract that trades raw efficiency for universality, operability and safe intermediaries.

scenes.voice: Why does almost every public API still use HTTP even though it's verbose and slow?
scenes.visual: Client icon on left, Server on right, with Proxy/CDN/LB icons between them. Question mark overlay.

scenes.voice: You have services in different languages, behind firewalls, proxies and CDNs. You need a reliable request-response contract that intermediaries can inspect, cache and route without knowing your business logic.
scenes.visual: Map of distributed services, different tech stacks, network with proxies.

scenes.voice: Custom binary RPC is efficient inside one org. It breaks at the public internet boundary because firewalls, caches and gateways can't reason about it.
scenes.visual: Binary blob hitting a firewall with red X, then HTTP text passing through.
scenes.on_screen_text: Binary RPC works inside. Breaks outside.

scenes.voice: HTTP is a stateless conversation about resources. Client sends method plus path plus headers plus body. Server replies with status plus headers plus body. State lives in the resource, not the connection.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    C[Client] -->|Request: method + path + headers + body| S[Server]
    S -->|Response: status + headers + body| C
    S -.-> P[Proxy / CDN / LB]

scenes.voice: The uniform interface lets proxies cache GETs, gateways enforce auth, and clients retry safely using status codes. Methods encode intent and idempotency is a contract, not an implementation detail.
scenes.visual: Gateway layer showing Auth, Rate Limit, Cache with arrows to service.

scenes.voice: You pay for this with overhead. Text is verbose, JSON is larger than protobuf, and request-response has no backpressure. You also push state out: sessions live in tokens or external stores.
scenes.visual: Scale up icons for services, with token and external store icons.

scenes.voice: So choose HTTP for public APIs and edge integration where you need caching, observability and independent evolution. Choose binary RPC for low-latency internal paths you control.
scenes.visual: Decision split: Public/Edge -> HTTP, Internal high-throughput -> gRPC.
scenes.on_screen_text: HTTP for edge, gRPC for internal

scenes.voice: HTTP optimizes for interoperability and operability, not raw speed. That's why it wins at the boundary.

mental_model: Think of HTTP as a stateless, uniform resource contract. Each request is self-contained with intent in the method and outcome in the status code. Intermediaries can reason about traffic without knowing business logic, which buys you operability at the cost of efficiency.
final_takeaway: Use HTTP when you need universality, caching and safe intermediaries; accept overhead for operability.
